newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Feb 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Feb 4.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- US TAKEOVER OF LONDON ELECTRIC CLEARED BY LANG

Entergy's 1.27 billion pounds stg bid for London Electricity has been cleared by Trade secretary Ian Lang. The decision will make the New Orleans based energy group the sixth US company to takeover a regional electricity company in the UK. The clearance, which was expected, came as Entergy reported it now had control of 71.1 percent of its target.
-- GULF SET TO OFFER 120P A SHARE FOR CLYDE

Gulf Canada is expected to raise is offer for Clyde Petroleum today from its original 105p a share, to 120p. This will upset investors who are hoping for substantially more. The new offer will value Clyde at 494 million pounds stg and is pitched at very near to Clyde's market price of 117.5p and will come on the very last day for an increased bid.
-- HALIFAX FINDS FALL IN HOUSE PRICES

According to the Halifax Building Society, house prices fell by 0.6 percent in January, a much sharper fall than expected. The society said the trend is still upwards, and that the fall could be due to the large rise in prices in December. The figures contradict a Nationwide Building Society claim that house prices rose by 0.7 percent in January.
THE TIMES
-- IVORY & SIME CHIEF QUITS OVER MANAGEMENT FALLOUT

The Edinburgh fund manager, Ivory & Sime, stated yesterday that it was not for sale, following the surprise departure of Colin Hook, its managing director. Hook resigned after a breakdown in his relationship with fund managers, four of whom resigned last month to set up their own firm. Ivory & Sime manages about 3.8 billion pounds stg and has a current market value of 78 million pounds stg.
-- OUTPUT BOOST UNLIKELY TO PUSH RATES UP

The latest survey from the Chartered Institute of Purchasing and Supply reveals an acceleration of growth in orders, output and employment in January. Growth was driven by domestic orders, especially in consumer goods. Despite the evidence of a pick up last month, the City still believes that Kenneth Clarke, the Chancellor, will maintain his resistance to Bank of England pressure for a rise in base rates.
-- MTM FOUNDER JAILED OVER 250 MILLION POUNDS FRAUD

Richard Lines, the founder and former chairman of MTM Plc, the chemicals group was yesterday starting a two year prison sentence for a fraud in which investors lost 250 million pounds stg. Lines was found guilty on two counts of conspiring to account falsely and one charge of making false or misleading statements. Thomas Baxter, the former finance director of MTM, was also sent to prison for six months for conspiring to account falsely and making false statements.
THE GUARDIAN
-- DTI INSIDER DEALING INQUIRY WIDENS TO RESTAURANT GROUP

The Department of Trade's inquiry into a suspected City insider dealing ring has widened to include trading in the shares of Greenhills, a restaurant group that went into receivership in December. Links are being examined between a Monaco based group of financiers and some shareholders in Greenhills, which was previously listed on the Alternative Investment Market.
-- AUDIT FIRM CALLS ITS RIVALS IN

KPMG, the accountancy firm, published its own audited accounts yesterday, revealing a 35 percent leap in profits to 24 million pounds stg. Accountancy firms are not legally required to disclose financial information but KPMG said the publication was part of a spirit of openness that would eventually become mandatory.
-- WIN DOUBLE AS LADBROKE BUYS BOOKIE AND SETTLES TEXAS ROW

Hotel and betting group Ladbroke strengthened its place as Britain's biggest bookmaker yesterday by buying the betting-shop chain AR Dennis for 31.3 million pounds stg. The group also announced it had resolved its dispute over the sale of Texas Homecare, the DIY chain, to Sainsbury in 1995. The disagreement was over the valuation of the chain and was referred to an independent expert last year. The value of the chain was lowered by 9.3 million pounds stg to 280.7 million pounds stg.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- INSTITUTIONS TALK TOUGH ON BALLOT BY SCOTAM

A meeting will be held next week between three UK fund managers with thousands of Scottish Amicable policies in their investment trusts, to discuss voting down the company's proposal for a two stage demutualisation. The three, Scottish Value Management, BZW and Kleinwort Benson want ScotAm to discuss takeover offers from bidders, which include Abbey National.
-- 154 MILLION POUNDS WIPED OFF DIXONS IN SHARE SALE FALL-OUT

Shares in Dixons fell 38p to 479p yesterday following Friday's share sale by Sir Stanley Kalms. The drop knocks 154 million pounds off the company's value. Investors were reacting to City talk that Merrill Lynch had changed its recommendations on the stock from hold to reduce. Merrill Lynch's move follows Sir Stanley's decision to sell a third of his holding in the company.
-- C&W SET TO PULL OUT OF GERMAN TELECOM TIE-UP

Cable & Wireless is thought to be ready to issue legal proceedings against RWE and Veba, the two partners in Vebacom its German telecommunications alliance, as speculation that it is ready to break its link with the venture grows. The dispute is thought to be over documents drawn up when RWE opted to join Vebacom. The three partners have not yet signed contracts formally to include RWE in Vebacom.
